claims.claim: ReproBrief 0.1.0 performs a real recipe-to-local-brief workflow on macOS arm64 with CPython 3.14.

evidence.result: success, unexpected-exit, mutation/redaction, interruption, and ZIP workflows passed

limitations: Local runtime evidence covers macOS 26.0 arm64 and CPython 3.14 only.

claims.claim: Recipe commands are strict argument arrays, are previewed before approval, and are executed without a shell.

evidence.reference: tests/test_config.py and tests/test_cli.py; 57-test run recorded in .product-incubator/evidence/release-readiness.md
evidence.result: unknown fields, shell-shaped inputs, traversal, nonapproval, and secret-bearing preview cases passed

limitations: Approved child programs are trusted and are not sandboxed.

claims.claim: stdout and stderr are concurrently drained with bounded retention; timeout and POSIX interruption clean up the tested process group.

evidence.result: 200,000-byte dual-stream, timeout descendant, exited-parent descendant, and real SIGINT cases passed

limitations: Windows descendant cleanup is bounded but does not use a Job Object and is not claimed as universal.

claims.claim: Generated persisted fields receive the documented best-effort path, explicit environment value, credential-shape, email, URL-credential, and private-key redaction.

evidence.result: seeded sensitive values were absent from every generated file

limitations: This verifies named transformations, not that arbitrary output is safe to share.
Transformed, split, encoded, novel, or semantically private values may remain.

claims.claim: Report publication refuses unrecognized or symbolic-link targets and replaces recognized output through a staged, recoverable path.

evidence.result: exclusive create, recognized force replace, unrecognized directory, symlink, and archive containment cases passed

limitations: The tool cannot make an arbitrary filesystem or failing disk atomic.

claims.claim: ReproBrief reports Git status before and after execution and does not automatically revert command side effects.

evidence.result: a real temporary worktree mutation appeared in the manifest and remained in the worktree

limitations: Git status metadata can contain sensitive filenames and is subject to redaction limits.

claims.claim: ReproBrief 0.1.0 has no third-party runtime dependencies.

evidence.result: wheel METADATA had no Requires-Dist and pip-audit 2.10.1 reported no known vulnerabilities for the empty runtime requirement set

limitations: Python, pip/build tooling, Git, the OS, PATH executables, and approved child commands remain supply-chain inputs.

claims.claim: The ReproBrief runtime contains no client networking or telemetry implementation and does not upload reports.

evidence.result: manual source/data-flow review plus Bandit 1.9.4 found no network client or persistence path outside requested local output

limitations: Approved child commands are outside this claim and can independently access the network or filesystem.

claims.claim: The repository supports CPython 3.11 and 3.14 on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

evidence.result: quality gate and all six OS/Python jobs passed, including install, 57 tests, CLI smoke, and wheel build

limitations: The supported matrix is bounded to CPython 3.11 and 3.14 on current GitHub-hosted Linux, macOS, and Windows images.

claims.claim: ReproBrief v0.1.0 is formally released with verified assets and checksums.
limitations: Requires an immutable remote tag, GitHub Release, checksums, and installation from GitHub.

claims.claim: External maintainers and reporters obtain useful value from ReproBrief.
limitations: No external-user trial has occurred; only non-fabricated post-release adoption targets are recorded.
